newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Garantia launches private equity fund.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Garantia launches private equity fund.

text.p: Banco de Investimentos Garantia launched a $300 million private equity fund designed to invest in less liquid Brazilian firms with good prospects for growth, a bank executive said.

"This fund aims to invest in companies which are less liquid on the bolsa but are well managed, with good investment projects and need capital and exposure to foreigners," Claudio Haddad, Garantia's executive, told a news conference on Monday.

Haddad said the fund will cover large companies, with annual revenues not lower than $80 million. The fund also may take part in privatizations as opportunities in ports, transportation, telecommunications and power sectors are expected for next year, he added.

Stakes in the fund were acquired by 16 domestic institutional investors, including four pension funds -- Previ, Centrus, Sistel and Petrus -- and BNDES Participacoes (BNDESPar), the investment arm of Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES). These five investors have acquired over 50 percent of the fund.
The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa) has also bought a $1 million stake in the fund.
Investors have already subscribed for $30 million and Garantia expects to reach $300 million in three years, said Marcelo de Medeiros, responsible for administering the fund.
Garantia already manages a $110 million private equity fund designed for foreign investors.
BNDESPar, which has invested $40 million in Garantia's fund, launched a special program to participate in private equity funds, said Durval Soledad, BNDESPar's representative.
Soledad said the institution has $200 million to invest in this type of funds.
